title: Give the dataloader object a heap identity (HEAP_SUBTYPE_DATALOADER) so its accessors can classify their operand, and teach the region evacuator its three interior pointers
goal: Close the one operand class that PR #365 (fix/tensor-operand-classification-sweep) could NOT fix by runtime-tag classification. dataloader-next / dataloader-reset! / dataloader-length / dataloader-has-next? each do `tagged_.unpackPtr(loader_tagged)` and then read fields 0..7 off the result. Unlike every other tensor operand, there is no tag to dispatch on: makeDataloader allocates the loader with plain `arena_allocate(arena, 64)` (lib/backend/tensor_dataloader_codegen.cpp:94-96) and packs the raw pointer with `tagged_.packPtr(loader_ptr, ESHKOL_VALUE_HEAP_PTR, 0)`, so the object carries NO eshkol_object_header_t and therefore no subtype byte. ESHKOL_GET_HEADER on it reads whatever arena bytes precede the allocation. Measured on PR #365's build: `(dataloader-length (vector 1.0 2.0 3.0))` returns 562262926385162 — a fabricated value assembled from the vector's bytes read as loader fields. It does not crash only because the read happens to land inside the arena. The fix is to give the loader a real identity, then classify against it.
background: PR #365 established the operand-classification family in lib/core/runtime_tensor_alloc.cpp: eshkol_tensor_operand_checked (read-only 1-D data, coerces a numeric vector/list), eshkol_tensor_destination_checked (written in place, rejects collections), eshkol_tensor_matrix_operand_checked (rank >= 2), eshkol_tensor_counts_checked (per-dimension counts), eshkol_tensor_axis_checked (reduction axis). All five dispatch on the object-header subtype. A sixth member for the dataloader is the natural shape of this fix, but it is blocked on the object having a header at all, which is why it was scoped OUT of #365 rather than guessed at.
next_actions: Add HEAP_SUBTYPE_DATALOADER = 26 to the eshkol_heap_subtype_t enum in inc/eshkol/eshkol.h (25 = HEAP_SUBTYPE_I128 is currently the highest). Follow the I128 precedent for how contained a new subtype can be: it touches only eshkol.h, its own runtime file, and runtime_display_hosted.cpp.

Switch makeDataloader (lib/backend/tensor_dataloader_codegen.cpp:94-96) from mem_.getArenaAllocate() to mem_.getArenaAllocateWithHeader() with subtype HEAP_SUBTYPE_DATALOADER and flags 0. The signature is `void* arena_allocate_with_header(arena_t*, size_t data_size, uint8_t subtype, uint8_t flags)` (see lib/backend/memory_codegen.cpp:70-72). Keep the 64-byte payload and the eight int64 field slots exactly as they are — this change is about the header, not the layout.

Add eshkol_dataloader_operand_checked(const eshkol_tagged_value_t*, const char* op_name) to lib/core/runtime_tensor_alloc.cpp beside its five siblings: return the pointer for a HEAP_PTR whose header subtype is HEAP_SUBTYPE_DATALOADER, otherwise eshkol_type_error_with_operand(op_name, "dataloader", val). No coercion — a dataloader is a stateful cursor, not data, so there is nothing to coerce FROM.

Route all four accessor sites through it: tensor_dataloader_codegen.cpp lines ~264 (dataloaderNext), ~465 (dataloaderReset), ~486 (dataloaderLength), ~519 (dataloaderHasNext). A small TensorCodegen helper mirroring checkReduceAxis is the cheapest wiring; do NOT extend TensorOperandMode, since that enum returns eshkol_tensor_t* and a loader is not a tensor.

HAZARD, do this deliberately: teach the region evacuator the loader's THREE interior pointers. Once the object has a header the evacuator will visit it, and evac_kind_for defaults an unrecognized subtype to a SHALLOW LEAF — which is precisely the ESH-0214d failure mode (see .swarm memory: evac_kind_for dropped KB/FACT/SUBSTITUTION/WORKSPACE to shallow leaf and left dangling interior pointers). The loader stores, as PtrToInt-encoded int64 in its field slots: field 0 = the data tensor (itself a HEAP_SUBTYPE_TENSOR object with its own dimensions and elements arrays), field 4 = the indices array (num_samples * 8 bytes, raw int64, no header), field 7 = the sample_dims array (sample_num_dims * 8 bytes, raw int64, no header). Fields 1/2/3/5/6 are plain scalars (batch_size, num_samples, current_idx, sample_size, sample_num_dims) and need no walking. A deep walk must evacuate the data tensor properly and copy the two raw arrays, then rewrite all three field slots with PtrToInt of the new addresses. Sizing the two raw arrays requires reading fields 2 and 6 first — they are not self-describing.

Handle the new subtype in runtime_display_hosted.cpp so `(display loader)` prints something honest (e.g. #<dataloader n-samples/batch-size>) rather than falling through to a default that may misread the payload.

Extend tests/ml/tensor_operand_classification_test.esk with the dataloader-identity block: a genuine loader still reports its length/has-next/next, and each of the four accessors raises catchably on a vector, a list, an integer, a string, and a TENSOR (a tensor is a heap object with a header, so it exercises the subtype check rather than the tag check). Assert the fabricated value is gone by name: (dataloader-length (vector 1.0 2.0 3.0)) must raise, not return 562262926385162.

Add a region-evacuation regression: create a dataloader inside a with-region, force evacuation, then iterate it to exhaustion and check the batches still hold the right values. This is the test that would have caught ESH-0214d for this object.
acceptance: All four dataloader accessors raise a catchable error naming the op for a vector/list/integer/string/tensor operand; none returns a fabricated value and none crashes.
A genuine dataloader round-trips unchanged: make-dataloader + dataloader-length + dataloader-has-next? + dataloader-next + dataloader-reset! all behave as before the change, in both JIT and AOT.

The loader survives region evacuation with all three interior pointers rewritten: the deep-walk regression iterates a post-evacuation loader to exhaustion and every batch value matches the pre-evacuation values.
(display loader) prints a dataloader-shaped form, not a misread payload.
ctest, scripts/run_ml_tests.sh, scripts/run_vm_parity.sh and the AD oracle/adversarial gates stay green; tests/ml/dataloader_test.esk in particular must not regress.
No consumer names and no AI attribution in any changed text.
notes: Scoped out of PR #365 on the coordinator's ruling: the fix is 'give this object an identity', not operand classification, and it carries a known hazard (the evacuator deep-walk) that deserves its own review. Not a v1.3.4 blocker.
Reproduce the current behavior in one line: (display (dataloader-length (vector 1.0 2.0 3.0))) => 562262926385162 on master and on #365.

The four call sites are the last `tagged_.unpackPtr` uses in lib/backend/tensor_*.cpp. The only other remaining one, tensor_conv_codegen.cpp:1189, is already correct — it fires only after checking base_type == ESHKOL_VALUE_CALLABLE and checkCallableSubtype(CALLABLE_SUBTYPE_AD_NODE).
